note: Repositories, file names, sizes, SHA-256 values and licences were checked against the Hugging Face API on 2026-11-22. An Apple pick with an evidence object was run on that machine with llama.cpp b12633 at the pick's window: the file loaded, answered and passed one tool-call check. peak_memory_gib is the server's peak memory to 0.1 GiB in the latest run (the higher of two runs for UD-Q6_K_XL), and file, where given, is the report of an earlier run of the same model file whose peak is within 0.1 GiB of it. It is evidence of loading, tool calling and memory use, not of speed. Apple picks without one are arithmetic estimates.

picks.why: The smallest model in the catalog, enough to try the app: about 3.7 GiB at a 16K window. No agentic-coding benchmark exists for it, so expect short edits only.
The smallest model in the catalog, enough to try the app. It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB with a 5.9 GiB peak at this window, more than an 8 GB Mac can spare.
Runs on the processor, so replies are slow; nothing was measured on a CPU build. The tool-call format works, but 9B models are unreliable on multi-step tasks.
For 8 GB cards: 6.4 GiB at a 16K window. The tool-call format works, but hands-on reports found 9B models unreliable for multi-step agent work.
For 12 GB cards: the highest-precision 9B file that keeps a 32K window, 8.55 GiB against 10.5 usable. Still a weak agent on multi-step tasks.
A 27B-class Strata pack its vendor says fits a 12 GB card. Not run here: its memory at this window and its tool calling are unverified, and it matches the original on 92.35% of next tokens.
For 16 GB cards: the 27B coding model at 3-bit precision, 12.2 GiB with a q8_0 cache at 32K. No evaluation exists at this precision, so its quality is unverified.
A 27B-class Strata pack its vendor reports on a 16 GB card. Not run here: 13.36 GiB of weights leaves little room for context, and its tool calling is unverified.
Measured at an 8K window only (12.15 GiB, one reply, no tool loop); the 16K window here is computed at 12.9 GiB. llama.cpp b12633 has open Inkling tool-call defects.
picks.measured_on: a Radeon RX 9070 XT (16 GB) on Linux

picks.why: The same file as the measured Pi adapter profile, but this plain launch is not measured and neither is a 24 GB card: 18.45 GiB computed with a q8_0 cache at 32K.
Measured on a 32 GB card at 32K with a two-turn tool exchange only; the 24 GB fit is computed at 19.3 GiB. llama.cpp b12633 has open Inkling tool-call defects.
The same file as the NVIDIA pick: 18.45 GiB computed with a q8_0 cache at 32K. Upstream reports show this model family serving under Vulkan on AMD cards; it is not measured here.
The daily preset this project was measured with: 157.6 tokens per second at 32K, with OMP edit loops and a vision check passed. Its memory at 32K was not recorded.
Best for long inputs and for Pi: measured at a 128K window with the Pi adapter and MTP drafting. It must run with thinking off, and its arithmetic and logic checks failed that way (3 of 5).
The highest-precision Inkling file for llama.cpp, measured at 32K. SQ-20 on Strata is faster and has the measured tool loops; llama.cpp b12633 has open Inkling tool-call defects.
The same file as the 24 GB pick with a 64K window: 19.45 GiB computed with a q8_0 cache. It is not measured on a Vulkan card.
Measured at 64K with an FP8 cache: a 49.6K-token retrieval passed at a 27.32 GiB peak on a 32 GB card. A 48 GB card itself was not measured.
The 27B coding model at 8-bit precision with a 128K window: 32 GiB computed with a q8_0 cache. It is not measured here.
The strongest model that fits by vendor numbers: 53.6 GiB computed at 64K with the n-gram shard read from disk. Not run here; tool calling on llama.cpp is unknown and the licence is conditional.
The same model with a 128K window: 55.05 GiB computed with the n-gram shard read from disk. Not run here; tool calling on llama.cpp is unknown and the licence is conditional.
It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB with an 8.6 GiB peak at this window, which is tight on a 16 GB Mac. A weak agent on multi-step tasks.
The 27B coding model at 3-bit precision. It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB with a 17.8 GiB peak at this window; no evaluation exists at 3 bits, so its quality is unverified.

Inkling 2 Mini at 4-bit precision on llama.cpp. It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB with a 20.5 GiB peak at this window, about all a 32 GB Mac can give; llama.cpp b12633 has open Inkling tool-call defects.
The 27B coding model at 4-bit precision. It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB with a 24.1 GiB peak at this window, which is tight on a 36 GB Mac.
The 27B coding model at 8-bit precision with a 128K window. Not run on a Mac: 33 GiB with a q8_0 cache is an arithmetic estimate, and the tested 27B files peaked up to 3.7 GiB above theirs.
The 27B coding model at 6-bit precision. It loads, answers and calls a tool on an M3 Max 48 GB, peaking at 27.5 to 29.5 GiB at this window across two runs, which left under 8 GiB free there.
The strongest model in the catalog by vendor numbers. Not run on a Mac: 56 GiB is an arithmetic estimate, tool calling on llama.cpp is unknown and the licence is conditional.
